issues.description: Predicate states an intent it does not encode: 'layer with no block' is not the same as 'typeof node.nodes === undefined'
issues.detail: The author wishes to distinguish a layer at-rule that introduces a block from one that does not. The chosen test 'typeof node.nodes === "undefined"' is a property check on a PostCSS-internal field, not a statement of the abstract property. A layer with an empty block `@layer foo {}` arrives with `nodes` defined as `[]`, while `@layer foo;` arrives with `nodes` undefined. The predicate happens to coincide with intent for the inputs the author tested, but the precondition is never stated: 'a layer at-rule has a block iff its `nodes` field is not undefined.' This is folklore-as-substitute-for-reasoning. Prefer an explicit, named predicate such as `node.nodes !== undefined` (or a helper `hasBlock(node)`), and document the invariant it relies on.

issues.description: Negated conjunction smuggled into a long disjunctive guard; the loop invariant of the surrounding check is nowhere stated
issues.detail: The surrounding expression is now a six-clause boolean composed of `isAtRule`, four name comparisons, an `optionsMatches`, and an `isStandardSyntaxAtRule`, with a fresh `!(A && B)` inserted in the middle. There is no stated invariant for what this predicate is computing. A reader must simulate the conjunction in their head to recover the intent, which is precisely the failure mode structured programming exists to prevent. Extract a named predicate `isDisallowedPrecedingNode(node)` whose precondition, postcondition, and the rule it enforces ('nothing other than @charset, @import, bodyless @layer, or ignored at-rules may precede @import') are stated once, in prose, above the function.

issues.description: Correctness rests on tests, not on a stated argument about the AST shape
issues.detail: The change is justified by one added test case ('layer block before import'). Tests of this kind show the presence of a bug in the prior version; they do not show the absence of bugs in the new one. There is no test for `@layer foo, bar;` (bodyless, multiple names), for `@layer {}` (anonymous block), for nested layer blocks, or for layer at-rules produced by syntax-extension plugins whose nodes property may differ. A short comment stating the AST invariant being relied on (PostCSS sets `nodes` to an array iff the at-rule has a block) would convert this from tested-not-proved to reasoned.

review.summary: The patch is small and behaviourally correct for the case it tests: a bodyless `@layer foo;` continues to be permitted before `@import`, while `@layer foo {}` is now rejected. It is, however, UNREASONED in the EWD sense. The author has not stated the precondition ('@import must be preceded only by @charset, @import, a bodyless @layer, or an ignored at-rule'), the AST invariant relied on ('PostCSS attaches a `nodes` array iff the at-rule has a block'), nor extracted the now-six-clause guard into a predicate whose intent a reader can grasp without simulating the expression. The fix is TESTED-NOT-PROVED: one added test demonstrates the prior bug; it does not demonstrate the absence of further ones (anonymous `@layer {}`, layer lists, plugin-produced nodes). Verdict: accept the behavioural change, but require that the guard be named, the predicate `node.nodes !== undefined` be written as such (not as `typeof ... === 'undefined'`), and the AST assumption be stated in a comment.
